scientific_goal: Find an economical 0p10 TCN63 fine-tuning objective that preserves the strong one-step and innovation statistics while keeping autonomous full-noise rollouts finite and statistically reasonable. Compare dense multi-horizon endpoint moments, low-particle multistep anchors, structured restoring+damping drift, identifiability/Lyapunov regularization, and cheap noisy-history augmentation under a hard 45-minute training limit per trial.
scientific_constraints: Every optimization starts from an explicitly named existing checkpoint. Never continue the nonfinite moment-only checkpoint. Preserve all source checkpoints and write every trial to this study's output root.
Use validation repetitions 13 and 14 for selection. Test repetitions 15 and 16 remain locked.

Each training subprocess has a hard 2700-second wall-clock limit. A timed-out partial directory is retained, marked failed, and must not be continued. Prefer fewer particles, fewer sampled windows, shared-horizon moment paths and one epoch over exceeding this limit.

The unstructured parent is the finite 50000-step velocity_h2_5_10_20_w0p1_e3 checkpoint. The structured parent is the TCN63 diagonal restoring+damping checkpoint whose original one-step training had good validation NLL but whose 5000-step rollouts became nonfinite; structured trials test whether economical closed-loop objectives can rescue it.

Moment-only means multistep likelihood weight zero; ordinary one-step NLL remains active because the current trainer always retains it. Dense moment horizons are 2,4,5,10,20,50,100 and share the same two generated paths through horizon 100.

Moment trajectory count denotes distinct observed starts, not likelihood particles. Each start always produces two independently noised generated paths. Keep 16 starts and a one-percent selected-batch fraction for the declared trials.

Economical multistep arms use only 8 or a pruned 16-to-4 particle schedule and at most a 0.5 percent example fraction. Treat their likelihoods as noisy stabilization signals, not accurate 21-dimensional density estimates.
Multistep gradients go to drift only. Mean-moment gradients go to drift; variance-moment gradients reach trainable drift and diffusion. One-step gradients continue to train both in joint mode.
All likelihood arms score all 21 coordinates at every declared horizon. Do not reduce mode counts to hide high-mode instability. Displacement multistep training remains excluded.

Use the optimized full-receptive-field TCN cache, indexed retained-window batches and recurrent-kernel compilation. Do not disable them to rescue a trial; compiler/runtime failures require review rather than silently changing the scientific recipe.

Screen every completed checkpoint for 25000 native validation steps with 4 conditions and 4 stochastic paths at full learned diffusion. Reject any nonfinite path, peak POD standardized RMS above 10, absolute standardized coordinate above 50, energy ratio outside [0.25,4], or POD covariance-trace ratio outside [0.25,4].

A passing 25000-step screen is evidence of boundedness, not proof. At most two candidates receive independent 50000-step, 8-condition by 4-path confirmation. Prefer candidates that also preserve one-step NLL and innovation whiteness and improve mean, covariance, energy and modal PSD jointly.

Run the eight queued trials before adaptive selection. The ninth and final training slot may be used only for one evidence-driven interpolation or ablation within the declared option space. Do not launch an unbounded hyperparameter search.
advisor_guidance: The TCN substantially improved local conditional statistics, but unconstrained one-step continuation and the first horizon-100 mean/variance fine-tune produced rare positive-feedback escapes. That failed moment run had two of sixteen 50000-step paths overflow after crossing roughly seven training standard deviations at steps 23443 and 47181. Its one-step validation NLL improved while the moment objective contribution was tiny and the stabilizing multistep loss had been removed. The stable unstructured parent survived its existing 32-path 50000-step confirmation, although its energy was high. Dense multi-horizon moments test whether short and intermediate endpoints supply enough generated-history feedback without likelihood particles. Low-particle likelihood arms test whether an inexpensive stabilization anchor is sufficient when moments carry the population statistics. The structured parent already failed without closed-loop training, so do not interpret structure alone as a solution; compare its combined arm with the regularized structured arm. History noise is a cheap exposure-bias intervention. Training speed and timeout are first-class evidence. Reject nonfinite or explosive screens immediately before plotting or innovations. Do not promote solely on finite trajectories or PSD appearance.

seed_runs.hypothesis: The multistep-trained unstructured TCN63 is the finite long-rollout parent whose local fit and stability should be preserved while correcting moments economically.
The explicit diagonal restoring+damping TCN has strong local prediction but its one-step-only 5000-step rollouts became nonfinite; closed-loop and regularized fine-tuning may rescue it.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Dense endpoint mean and variance targets from 2 through 100 steps may preserve generated-history behavior without a likelihood particle cloud.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Finish well within 45 minutes, improve multi-horizon moment errors and remain finite for 25000 steps without materially degrading one-step NLL.

initial_trials.hypothesis: A stronger dense moment objective may exert enough influence to counter the always-active one-step likelihood.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Larger moment improvement than weight 0.03 without opening a rare unstable tail or damaging innovation calibration.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Eight likelihood particles on 0.5 percent of windows can retain the parent's stabilizing feedback while dense moments carry ensemble statistics.
initial_trials.expected_observation: A sub-45-minute stable screen competitive with the parent and better moment statistics than the likelihood-only source.

initial_trials.hypothesis: The source multistep weight may remain necessary even with only eight particles when moments supply a lower-variance population target.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Greater stability than weight 0.03 with acceptable local NLL and without excessive energy.

initial_trials.hypothesis: A pruned 16-to-4 particle schedule extending likelihood feedback to 50 steps may stabilize rare excursions more efficiently than many particles at short horizons.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Remain under the runtime cap and improve late-rollout boundedness relative to the short p8 arm.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Explicit positive restoring and damping operators plus economical generated-history objectives may rescue the previously unstable structured TCN.
initial_trials.expected_observation: A finite 25000-step screen with explicit operator contributions retained and local NLL near the structured parent.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Joint diagonal residual orthogonality plus a weak two-step Lyapunov penalty can keep the residual from cancelling the explicit stable core.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Better amplitude control than the matched unregularized structured arm without timeout or severe one-step degradation.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Noisy history reconstruction is a cheap way to teach recovery from slightly off-manifold TCN contexts while dense moments constrain generated endpoints.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Moment-only runtime with fewer rare excursions than the matched dense-moment arm and preserved one-step innovation quality.
